content.value_statement: Developers need reliable ADK patterns when building Python agents. This skill provides concise references for tools, callbacks, state, multi-agent orchestration, and workflow code.
actual_capabilities: Shows Python ADK agent definitions with model, instruction, tools, callbacks, and output keys.
Explains custom tool patterns, ToolContext state access, and function documentation rules.
Covers SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent, and remote agent patterns.
References ADK workflow nodes, edges, resume behavior, context properties, and replayable state updates.
Directs users to related Google agents-cli skills for scaffolding, workflow, evaluation, and deployment.
limitations: This skill focuses on Python ADK code and does not cover other languages.
It is a reference guide and does not create a project by itself.
Deployment guidance is delegated to the related deploy skill.
Deep API details may require checking official ADK documentation or installed package sources.

use_cases.title: Create a First ADK Agent
use_cases.description: Use the basic Agent pattern to define a Python root agent with tools and clear instructions.

use_cases.title: Add Tools and State
use_cases.description: Use ToolContext, docstrings, and typed functions to connect agent logic with application state.

use_cases.title: Design Multi-Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Choose sequential, parallel, loop, or graph workflow patterns for more complex agent systems.

prompt_templates.title: Start an Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple Python ADK agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a simple Python ADK agent for my use case: [describe task]. Include the agent name, model, instruction, and one tool.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Tool
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate tool design with state awareness.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a typed ADK tool for [capability]. Show the docstring, ToolContext usage if needed, and expected return shape in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Agent Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to choose an ADK orchestration pattern for [workflow]. Compare sequential, parallel, and loop options, then recommend one.

prompt_templates.title: Review Advanced Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for workflow state and resume behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my ADK workflow design for state handling, human-in-the-loop resume behavior, and replay safety. Identify concrete fixes.

output_examples.input: Build an ADK weather assistant with one lookup tool.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a root agent, a typed weather tool, a clear instruction, and notes about tool docstrings and return fields.

output_examples.input: I need three specialists to run in parallel and combine results.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a ParallelAgent inside a SequentialAgent, names distinct output keys, and describes the merge step.

output_examples.input: Review my workflow that pauses for user approval.
output_examples.output: The response checks resume inputs, interrupt identifiers, replayable state updates, and the node behavior after human approval.

best_practices: Scaffold or enhance the project before writing ADK agent code.
Use clear tool docstrings and type hints because the model sees them.
Use unique output keys and interrupt identifiers in parallel or resumable flows.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for project creation when the scaffold skill is required.
Do not place deployment decisions in this skill when the deploy skill is available.
Do not mutate workflow state directly when an event-based update is replayable.

faq.question: What language does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python ADK patterns. Other languages are outside this skill.

faq.question: Can it create a new ADK project?
faq.answer: No. Use the related scaffold skill for project creation or project enhancement.

faq.question: Does it include deployment guidance?
faq.answer: No. Use the related deploy skill for Cloud Run, GKE, CI, and production deployment work.

faq.question: What agent patterns are included?
faq.answer: It covers basic Agent setup, tools, callbacks, state, sequential flows, parallel flows, loops, and remote agent references.

faq.question: When should I use the workflow reference?
faq.answer: Use it when the agent needs explicit graph topology, human review, fan-out, fan-in, or resumable execution.

faq.question: Does it replace official ADK documentation?
faq.answer: No. It provides concise patterns and points to official documentation for deeper API details.
